clue.text: Role old VIP played without director in team

indicators.note: played signals the letters of role, old and VIP being performed in a new order
without says a letter must be left out of that pool of letters

explanation.surface: An actor takes an old VIP role on stage, with no director, in a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLE OLD VIP has ten letters; 'without' removes the D for director, and 'played' rearranges the remaining nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool FC is a famous English football club, so the city name stands for the side.

clue.text: Sneering look about head of police, despised person

indicators.note: about means the look goes round the other letter

parts.note: a leer is a sly or sneering look

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word police

explanation.surface: A man sneers at the police chief, whom he despises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P (first letter of 'police') inside LEER.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast shunned by society is figuratively called this, from the sufferers of the disease once isolated.

clue.text: See guy mixed up with trial showing coarse nature

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: mixed up signals that the letters of guy and trial are jumbled

explanation.surface: Watch a fellow embroiled in a court case revealing his crude character.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from vide, used in footnotes; 'mixed up' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudeness or lack of refinement is the quality described by this noun.

clue.text: Highly aggressive sort taking out note from letter in row possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of letter, in and row may be rearranged
taking out says a letter is removed from that pool

explanation.surface: Someone fierce removes a note from a letter during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: LETTER IN ROW has eleven letters; 'taking out' drops N for note and 'possibly' rearranges the other ten. 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This German breed of dog is known as powerful and potentially fierce, a highly aggressive sort.

clue.text: Crime of sportsman curtailed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a fencer is a sportsman who duels with foils or sabres

explanation.surface: A sportsman whose career was cut short committed a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' removes the final R from FENCER to give FENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An illegal act or breach of law is a synonym for a crime.

clue.text: Person on ship's worry

definitions.meaning: a sailor posted to watch for danger or land
as in 'that's your own concern', meaning someone's responsibility or worry

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck frets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor on watch keeps this post, and 'that's your lookout' means it is your problem to handle.

clue.text: Pallid like layer?

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a hen is a layer, a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is as pale as a stratum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' suggests a stratum, but here it means something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey and pale like wood residue from a fire, so pallid in complexion.

clue.text: Star typecast in part as an aesthete?

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film star always typecast in the role of a lover of beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone with pretensions to artistic taste, as an aesthete might be.

clue.text: Leaders of hostile armies invaded famous ancient city

indicators.note: leaders of picks the first letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: The heads of enemy forces invaded a renowned old city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'hostile armies invaded famous ancient' spell the city; 'Leaders of' looks like it refers only to the armies.
explanation.definitionFit: This port is a major city in northern Israel, on Mount Carmel.

clue.text: Philosopher cites Zen in work around middle of metaphysics

indicators.note: around means the anagram goes round the single middle letter
in work signals that the letters of cites and Zen are worked into a new order
middle of picks the central letter of the word metaphysics

explanation.surface: A thinker quotes Zen in a treatise on metaphysics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in work' makes NIETZSCE, and 'around' wraps it round the centre of 'metaphysics'; the anagram splits so the H lands second from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was a nineteenth-century German thinker, author of Thus Spoke Zarathustra.

clue.text: Experimental programme showing story about Italy

indicators.note: about means the story goes round the other letter

parts.note: a plot is the storyline of a tale
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A trial TV show tells a tale set in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside PLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial episode made to test a television series is called this.

clue.text: Interviewer with incisive quality hazard faced by explorer?

parts.note: Sir David Frost was a famous British television interviewer
bite means sharpness or cutting force

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued journalist is a danger to someone exploring.
explanation.walkthrough: David Frost was a well-known British TV interviewer, famous for his Nixon interviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar explorers risk freezing damage to fingers and toes, a classic hazard of extreme cold.

clue.text: Old film, reward I won after struggle

indicators.note: after struggle signals that the letters of reward, I and won are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of winning a prize after a hard fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after struggle' is the anagram signal; the 1954 Hitchcock film is the 'old film'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1954 thriller with James Stewart is a classic motion picture.

clue.text: Music coming from joint with a sleepy sound

parts.note: J is slang shorthand for a cannabis joint
zz represents the sound of snoring

explanation.surface: Drowsy tunes drifting out of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a nightclub, but gives J.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre born in New Orleans with improvisation and swing is a style of popular music.

clue.text: Writer in morning engaged in drinks

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside the other word

parts.note: martinis are cocktails, so drinks
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A novelist starts on cocktails before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' is the container signal; 'drinks' suggests a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The British novelist of Money and London Fields is an author, so a writer.

clue.text: Foolish error in state primarily forgotten

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
primarily forgotten means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Maine is a US state
a sin is a wrongdoing or error

explanation.surface: A silly mistake in the state's records is forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily forgotten' leaves AINE, and 'in' sets the wrongdoing inside it; Maine is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or senseless behaviour is described by this adjective, from the Latin for donkey.

clue.text: Wren, say, getting order in time when up before court

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
in means the order goes inside the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a chit is a note or written order

explanation.surface: A bird receives a command at the time it rises before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when up' reverses the period to ARE in this down clue, and 'in' sets the order inside it. Wren is Sir Christopher Wren, designer of St Paul's Cathedral, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren was a famous building designer, an example of the profession.

clue.text: A fine fellow engaged in mostly instant dealings

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside the other piece
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A good man gets involved in quick business transactions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TRICE to TRIC, and 'engaged in' puts AFF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit trade, as in drug trafficking, means commercial dealings.

clue.text: Young one in flight from Florida progressing slowly around lake

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

indicators.note: around means the edging word goes round the lake letter

parts.note: edging means moving forward gradually

explanation.surface: A youngster flies out of Florida, inching round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal. 'Flight' suggests an escape from Florida, but defines a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird that has just grown feathers and started to fly is so called.

clue.text: Company head around yard revealing evasive quality

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A firm's boss shows a shy streak near the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal. 'Head' looks like a company chief, but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shy or coquettishly reluctant to commit is a kind of evasiveness.

clue.text: Entertainment cancelled for vain figure

parts.note: a show is an entertainment
off means cancelled, as an event that is off

explanation.surface: A performance was called off because of a conceited star.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flaunts themselves to attract admiration is vain and boastful.

clue.text: Road feature as yet to be developed in case of Cheshire

indicators.note: in means the anagram sits inside the outer letters
case of picks the outer letters, first and last, of Cheshire
to be developed signals that the letters of as yet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A highway reflector remains to be built in a Cheshire case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be developed' rearranges AS YET into ATSEY, and 'in' puts it between C and E, the first and last letters of Cheshire. Cheshire is an English county, and the Cheshire Cat hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflective stud set into the road surface to mark lanes at night has this name.

clue.text: One supplying cheer, note, embraced by support at home?

indicators.note: embraced by means the note is held inside the other word

parts.note: a carer looks after someone in their home
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A source of good cheer embraces music and home help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' is the container signal. 'Cheer' here means food and drink, as in 'Christmas cheer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who provides food and drink for events supplies good cheer in the old sense of fare.

clue.text: Foreign character, one facing register right away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: a rota is a list or register of duties

explanation.surface: A foreigner, solo, faces signing up immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from ROTA to leave OTA. 'Foreign character' is a letter of a foreign alphabet, not a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: House in Stroud designed with no end of fuss

indicators.note: designed signals the letters of Stroud being arranged into a new form
no says a letter is left out of that pool
end of picks the last letter of the word fuss

explanation.surface: A house in a Gloucestershire town was built without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of fuss' drops S from STROUD, and 'designed' rearranges the rest. Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the English royal dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, a royal house.

clue.text: Sort of record broken by figure, say, with rule in country

indicators.note: broken by means the record word is split by the pieces that follow

parts.note: a mono record is one in single-channel sound
ten is a number, so a figure
eg, for example, is signalled by say
R is an abbreviation for rule, as in rex or regina

explanation.surface: A broken disc is cited as an example with a rule in a land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' splits the record type to take the three pieces inside; 'say' is the usual signal for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balkan state on the Adriatic became independent in 2006, a nation.

clue.text: Some cricket beginning to thrill public

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word thrill

explanation.surface: A bit of cricket to start thrilling the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is six balls bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and not hidden, as a public display, is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Beware part of rocky coastline?

definitions.meaning: a hollow in a cliff face along the shore

explanation.surface: A warning about a stretch of rugged shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep cave' is old British school slang for keeping a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for beware is used in English slang, and a hollow in a sea cliff is a typical feature of the shore.

clue.text: Cook's associated with this attempt

definitions.meaning: Captain James Cook sailed his ship of this name to Australia

explanation.surface: A navigator is linked to this undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is Captain James Cook, whose ship HMS Endeavour reached Australia in 1770.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Endeavour was Captain Cook's famous vessel, and the word also means a serious effort.

clue.text: Something cultivated state of confusion in audience

indicators.note: in audience means as heard by listeners, a sound-alike

parts.note: a maze is a bewildered state, as in 'in a maze'

explanation.surface: Something grown leaves the crowd bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: MAZE sounds the same as the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal crop, also called corn, is grown on farms worldwide.

clue.text: Brief part of chapter seen

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a short piece of the chapter was viewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and to the point in speech or writing means concise.

clue.text: Vision in support of location, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: for means in favour of; a site is a location

explanation.surface: Seeing support for a place, by report.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR SITE, said together, sounds like the answer: both halves are sound-alikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning wisely for the future shows foresight, i.e. far-sighted vision.
